P1 — NAMED.md:7 — `M329` row 3 “exactly one `.text` ref” and “only string” are ungated.
`NAMED.md:7` marks the row VERIFIED against `G11`, but `scripts/m329_scratchtree.py` only checks the in-frame tag call: `len(tw) == 1`, `GONAME in pushes`, `TAGSIZE in pushes`, the 65-B offset, and one context-opener call. It never scans image-wide text for `0x6899ec`, never counts `.text` refs, and never enumerates frame strings. Therefore the “only string” / “only `.text` ref” facts cannot fail under this gate; `MU22`–`MU24` only perturb the known in-frame call. Why it matters: a V claim about global naming evidence is not backed by the cited measurement.

P1 — NAMED.md:9 — `[rec+0x38]` census rows cite wrong constants/addresses and the gate reads a different field.
`NAMED.md:9` claims defaults `0xdfbe41 @0x59ed6c` and `0xdfbe01 @0x5a0510`, and `0x59ed40` as the copying reader. The actual printed census at `evidence/m329_scratchtree.txt` T5 shows writers `0x59ed6c,0x59ed7a` with constants `0xdfbe41,0xc0dfbe41`, no `0x5a0510` row, and the copying reader cited by G9 as `0x4e494c`. `scripts/m329_scratchtree.py` also pins `PIN_CONSTS = {0xDFBE41, 0xC0DFBE41}` and does not measure `[rec+0x38]` image-wide; it greps absolute `0x94d600` forms only. Why it matters: a “VERIFIED bits” row is stale/contradicted by its own evidence and does not measure the prose’s exact displacement.

P1 — NAMED.md:9 / scripts/m329_scratchtree.py:609 — “writer census exact displacement” is a substring/global-address census, not a `+0x38` census.
The prose says `[rec+0x38]` writer census with exact displacement plus the `0x41ad94` fold. In `scripts/m329_scratchtree.py` T5, refs are selected by `hex(FIELD) in t`, i.e. any line containing `0x94d600`, and classified W/R by whether `0x94d600` appears in operand 0. It does not parse base/index/displacement, does not verify block+0x38, and does not include the dynamic `[reg+0x38]` stores or read-copies the claim references. Why it matters: the gate validates the wrong address form; the “image-wide exact displacement” claim is not computed from bytes.

P1 — scripts/m329_scratchtree.py:360 / NAMED.md:13 — write-back “19 test/or pairs + 1 clear” is not gated; the instrument reports many “no direct op” legs.
`G6` only requires `len(reads) == 19`, distinct pack masks/bits, scratch bit span, or/and agreement for pack legs, and that resolved restored bits are inside the pack mask set (`not outside`). It never proves 19 write-back `test scratch,bit` → `or [rec+0x38],mask` pairs, never counts the clear, and the printed evidence shows multiple “no direct op” write-back legs (`evidence/m329_scratchtree.txt`). Why it matters: the mutation harness can keep the row green even if most write-back pairings disappear; the prose claims a complete 19-pair tree.

P1 — NAMED.md:6 — call-site retraction adds “0 jmps” and “sole 6899ec immediate” without any instrument output.
The row says the image-wide dump has zero jmps to the frame and only one `6899ec` immediate. `scripts/m329_scratchtree.py` T1 decodes only `E8` relative calls; there is no jmp-target scan and no image-wide immediate grep for `0x6899ec`. The evidence file has no line for those facts. Why it matters: these are decisive retraction facts but cannot be reddened by the named harness and should not be V under the shipped gate.

P1 — NAMED.md:7 / scripts/m329_scratchtree.py:307 — three-chain row asserts fields/counts/sorts that G3 does not measure.
`NAMED.md:7` claims `+3584`, count bounds `1..37`, rank `1..3` with “0 refuses (4 sites)”, `FUN_005e5580` index sort, `FUN_00434190` over `[ebp-0x44]`, and cap `[ebp-0x48]`. `G3` only checks three frame chains, stride `304`, fields subset of `{0x4,0x78}`, and `304 % 52 != 0`. It does not measure count, rank, sort callees, cap, or `+3584`; the printed chains actually resolve to record offsets `0x4` and `0x78`, not `3584`. Why it matters: most of the named-row payload is decorative and can be false while G3 passes.

P2 — NAMED.md:6 — “exactly 4 call sites” misses indirect-call/jmp coverage.
`scripts/m329_scratchtree.py` finds only direct `E8` calls by decoding rel32. It does not scan `FF /2` indirect calls, jump tables, or `jmp` tails, and `NAMED.md:6` explicitly leans on “0 jmps” as supporting the site count. Why it matters: “exactly 4” should either be weakened to “4 direct `E8` sites” or backed by a real indirect-edge census; otherwise the call-site count can overstate confidence.

P2 — scripts/m329_scratchtree.py:312 — “read of shown page” is really “any operand with displacement 0x3ff3c”.
`T2`/`G2` count any instruction whose parsed memory displacement equals `SHOW` or `CURSOR`; it does not verify mnemonic direction or that the memory operand is a source rather than destination. The claim in `NAMED.md:12`/`NAMED.md:7` is about reads. Why it matters: a store or `lea`-like operand using the same displacement would be counted as a read; the gate should classify instruction polarity from opcode/modrm.

P2 — scripts/m329_scratchtree.py:418 — publish-mask gate does not pin the publish address.
`G7` extracts the first `and ecx,imm` in the frame (`andmask[0]`) and checks it is `0xf000000`, but it never asserts that this `and` is at `0x41abdc` or associated with the publish store. `PIN_PUBLISH` is checked for the store in `G5`, not for the mask. Why it matters: the claim’s endpoint is the gating mask at the publish path; another in-frame `and ecx,0xf000000` would satisfy G7 while making the address-specific claim false.

P2 — scripts/m329_scratchtree.py:250 — scratch-bit extraction for the sbb-dance leg is hardcoded.
For any leg containing `sbb`, the code sets `sbit = 0x1` unconditionally (`scripts/m329_scratchtree.py:382` in the leg loop) while claiming the permutation is measured. A mutation that changes the first scratch bit’s construction could still preserve distinctness/span depending on later legs, but the leg’s claimed scratch bit is not independently read from the instruction stream. Why it matters: one permutation leg is asserted by a literal in the instrument rather than by the bytes, weakening the “permutation” V claim.
